Stanford Cardinal.previous_hc_experience: None. The Coaching Carousel records that Tavita Pritchard played for the Cardinal from 2006-09 and coached for them from 2011-22, and has spent the last three seasons with the Commanders coaching up quarterbacks, including Jayden Daniels. The team pages call him a first-time head coach.
Stanford Cardinal.oc: Terry Heffernan, a first-time coordinator, in a role titled Andrew Luck Director of Offense.
Stanford Cardinal.dc: Kris Richard, a longtime NFL coordinator and defensive backs coach, titled David Shaw Director of Defense.
Stanford Cardinal.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Stanford Cardinal.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Stanford Cardinal.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Stanford Cardinal.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide notes Heffernan has spent much of his career coaching offensive lines, which it calls a good thing here, and that all three quarterback options are more mobile than their predecessors.
Stanford Cardinal.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but characterised: the guide describes a complex NFL-caliber scheme and offers a genuine advantage — Stanford has a lot of smart players who should grasp it.
Stanford Cardinal.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Stanford Cardinal.qb_development: The one specific coaching credit the guide offers. It notes Pritchard has worked with Jayden Daniels over recent seasons and spent five years as Commanders coordinator, so he may get something from one of the quarterback options — Davis Warren, Ben Gulbranson, UCF transfer Dylan Rizk or true freshman Mike Mitchell.
Stanford Cardinal.continuity: None on the staff or at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 3 for 14 returning starters, totalling 3.
Stanford Cardinal.staff_turnover: Complete, following Frank Reich's stopgap season. The guide records Reich having responded to Andrew Luck's plea to serve as a stopgap last season, with Pritchard, Heffernan and Richard all new.
Stanford Cardinal.prior_school: Stanford itself for Pritchard, who played and coached there. The Washington Commanders for his most recent role, and the NFL generally for Kris Richard, who the guide notes has not worked in college since a graduate assistant role at USC in 2008-09.
Stanford Cardinal.portal_recruiting: Identified as a structural constraint rather than a staff choice. The guide says high academic requirements make the portal far less of a shopping spree than at other schools and expects that to hold the programme back again, while recording a $50 million NIL collective donation in October 2025 from former player Bradford Freeman and a revenue-sharing model instituted in spring 2025.
Stanford Cardinal.vsin_assessment: Unimpressed with the hire, and explicit about the difficulty of the job. The Coaching Carousel says in retrospect we do not give enough credit to Jim Harbaugh and David Shaw for what they did at Stanford, and that replicating it in today's NIL era would be one of the best coaching jobs we have ever seen — then says 'unimaginative' is the best way to describe the hire. It notes that even with the weight a Stanford degree carries, Andrew Luck and now Pritchard know the academic requirements in Palo Alto severely limit the player pool. The team pages leave open whether Luck can turn the programme and call the roster underwhelming again.
Stanford Cardinal.strengths: A head coach with deep programme roots and three seasons developing NFL quarterbacks including Jayden Daniels, an offensive coordinator whose background is coaching offensive lines on a team that has allowed 31, 41, 41, 39 and 41 sacks over five years, a defensive coordinator with long NFL experience, a roster of smart players the guide says should grasp a complex scheme, and a $50 million NIL donation behind it.
Stanford Cardinal.concerns: A Stability Score of 3 with a first-time head coach, a first-time offensive coordinator and a defensive coordinator who has not worked in college since 2009; a turnover margin of -33 over five years; a sack differential of -83 over five seasons; and academic requirements the guide says severely limit the player pool.
Stanford Cardinal.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Stanford Cardinal.carousel_summary: Adam Burke begins by looking backward: in retrospect, he does not think we give enough credit to Jim Harbaugh and David Shaw for what they did at Stanford, and says if somebody can replicate that in today's NIL era it will be one of the best coaching jobs we have ever seen. He records the resources — a $50 million donation in October 2025 from former player Bradford Freeman, and a revenue-sharing model instituted in spring 2025 — then the constraint: even with the weight that a Stanford degree carries, Andrew Luck and now Pritchard, who played for the Cardinal from 2006-09 and coached for them from 2011-22, know the academic requirements in Palo Alto severely limit the player pool. He notes Pritchard has spent the last three seasons with the Commanders coaching up QBs, including Jayden Daniels. His verdict is one word: 'unimaginative' is the best way to describe the hire after Frank Reich responded to Luck's plea to serve as a stopgap last season.

Syracuse Orange.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide for Fran Brown. The guide does record the incoming defensive coordinator's: Vince Kehres was Mount Union's head coach, going 95-6 in Division III with two national championships, before six seasons as Toledo's coordinator.
Syracuse Orange.dc: Vince Kehres, the former Mount Union head coach and Toledo coordinator.
Syracuse Orange.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Syracuse Orange.dc_status: New — the guide records the Kehres hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Syracuse Orange.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Syracuse Orange.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but the guide treats fit within it as decisive: Steve Angeli posted a 10-to-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio thriving in Jeff Nixon's system, while his replacements went 7 to 13.
Syracuse Orange.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide characterises Kehres by output at Toledo, where the Rockets allowed between 13.3 and 25.1 points per game and exceeded 5.0 yards per play only once.
Syracuse Orange.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Syracuse Orange.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide keeps the uncertainty about Angeli open in both directions — a three-star freshman in 2022 and a three-star transfer in 2025 per 247Sports who may simply have been thriving in his first real chance to start.
Syracuse Orange.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes, as does the special teams coordinator. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 13.
Syracuse Orange.staff_turnover: Two hires the guide treats as upgrades: Vince Kehres on defense, which it rates as possibly one of the best of the coaching cycle, and special teams coordinator Alex Bayer from Bowling Green.
Syracuse Orange.prior_school: Mount Union and Toledo for Kehres; Bowling Green for Bayer; Notre Dame for quarterback Steve Angeli. The guide also records Amari Odom having started at Kennesaw State and Malachi Nelson being on his fourth team.
Syracuse Orange.portal_recruiting: Credited historically — the guide notes Fran Brown assembled a spectacular portal class before the 10-3 season of 2024 — while recording that Angeli faces an entirely new receiver group, the top returnee having caught eight passes.
Syracuse Orange.vsin_assessment: A collapse attributed largely to one injury, with three specific fixes stacked against it. The guide argues no injury was more impactful than losing Angeli, records the eight-game losing streak by 35, 13, 17, 25, 17, 28, 63 and 22 points, and attributes the decline partly to a -13 turnover margin and -17 sack margin. It rates the Kehres hire as possibly one of the best of the cycle. On special teams it presents genuinely conflicting evidence rather than resolving it — Phil Steele's rankings had Syracuse 131st and 100th in the Brown era while Bill Connelly's SP+ had them 35th, which it calls a massive discrepancy.
Syracuse Orange.strengths: A returning quarterback whose four starts produced a 10-to-2 ratio in a system he thrived in, offensive-coordinator continuity, a defensive coordinator with two Division III national titles and six years of strong Toledo defenses, a new special teams coordinator, and a head coach with a proven portal class behind him.
Syracuse Orange.concerns: A defense that allowed 34.9 points and 6.5 yards per play — worse than the 1-10 COVID season — conceding 30 or more in seven of the final eight games and 70 to Notre Dame; an entirely new receiver group whose top returnee caught eight passes; and a quarterback whose four-start sample the guide will not treat as settled.
Syracuse Orange.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching. Its coaching-linked conclusion is directional: better field position with a healthy offense and improved defense could make Syracuse better in all three phases.

Virginia Cavaliers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Tony Elliott winning 11 games total across his first three seasons before last year's 11-3.
Virginia Cavaliers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Virginia Cavaliers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Virginia Cavaliers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Virginia Cavaliers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide traces the turnaround to a specific investment in the offensive line, which cut sacks allowed from 47 to 18 and raised yards per carry from 3.7 to 4.6.
Virginia Cavaliers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide offers a mechanism for the improvement — it came in Rudzinski's second year, so players may simply have learned the scheme.
Virginia Cavaliers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Virginia Cavaliers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Chandler Morris leaving after 3,000 yards and a 16-to-9 ratio, with Penn State and Missouri transfer Beau Pribula plus Pitt transfer Eli Holstein arriving.
Virginia Cavaliers.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 3 for 14 returning starters, totalling 13.
Virginia Cavaliers.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Virginia Cavaliers.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Beau Pribula from Penn State by way of Missouri and Eli Holstein from Pitt.
Virginia Cavaliers.portal_recruiting: Assessed unevenly by side of the ball. 247Sports ranks Virginia's portal class eighth in the ACC, including running back Peyton Lewis and receiver Da'Shawn Martin, and the guide judges the defensive portal haul more proven than the offensive one.
Virginia Cavaliers.vsin_assessment: A breakthrough credited to a specific decision, then interrogated. The guide traces the turnaround to the offensive line investment and the 8.1-point rise in scoring and 9.2-point defensive improvement that followed, then poses the burning question plainly — one-year flash or something more. It supplies evidence Virginia was genuinely good, being +98, +124 and +11 in yardage in its three losses and outgained only three times, all in wins. It then applies 'cluster luck', borrowed from Joe Peta's Trading Bases, to third-down conversion rate — 11th on offense and second on defense, with nearly twice as many offensive third-down conversions as opponents and 35 more in conference games, plus 163 more plays run — and ends on the open question of whether any of it repeats.
Virginia Cavaliers.strengths: Both coordinators returning after an 11-3 season and the conference's only 7-1 league record, an offensive line that remains mostly intact after transforming the team's numbers, four of the top six tacklers back, and a defensive portal haul the guide calls more proven than the offensive one.
Virginia Cavaliers.concerns: Virtually everyone else on offense being new, which the guide names as the major concern; the loss of a 1,000-yard rusher who was also fourth in receptions with everyone ahead of him also gone; the loss of both top pass rushers and the leading tackler; and situational numbers the guide doubts will repeat, noting 31 sacks last season after 30 in the previous two combined.
Virginia Cavaliers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Virginia Tech Hokies.previous_hc_experience: Extensive, and central to the guide's projection. The Coaching Carousel records James Franklin at 8-7 in bowl games and 2-1 in the CFP with a very high regular-season floor: two 9-4 seasons at Vanderbilt in the early 2010s when that was a rough job, and six double-digit winning seasons at Penn State.
Virginia Tech Hokies.dc: Brent Pry, retained — the guide records Franklin keeping him as coordinator.
Virginia Tech Hokies.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Virginia Tech Hokies.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator. The guide's own framing is retention of a person rather than continuity of a role: Franklin kept Brent Pry as coordinator, a perfect-storm situation given their long association that should ease the leadership transition.
Virginia Tech Hokies.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Virginia Tech Hokies.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records the offense managing only 21.4 points per game but 4.9 yards per carry even with Kyron Drones dragging the average down, so Franklin could focus on skill positions rather than rebuilding the line, and expects Marcellous Hawkins to feature more without a running quarterback.
Virginia Tech Hokies.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Virginia Tech Hokies.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Virginia Tech Hokies.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Penn State transfer Ethan Grunkemeyer having started seven games there and having chemistry with new tight end Luke Reynolds, alongside North Carolina transfer Bryce Baker.
Virginia Tech Hokies.continuity: None as printed, though the guide argues otherwise in substance. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 4 for 17 returning starters, totalling 4. The guide separately asks whether continuity can be quantified, answers probably not directly, and argues Franklin gained trust from players and respect from the athletic department by retaining Brent Pry.
Virginia Tech Hokies.staff_turnover: Complete at the top but softened by one deliberate retention. The guide records the defense avoiding a mass exodus, with four of the top six tacklers back plus many who played in some capacity, and notes several Penn State players followed Franklin.
Virginia Tech Hokies.prior_school: Penn State, comprehensively — Franklin, quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer, tight end Luke Reynolds and several other players. The Carousel adds that Franklin is a southeastern PA native who should recruit well in the DMV and the Keystone State. The guide also records Bryce Baker from North Carolina, Que'Sean Brown from Duke and Jaquez White from Troy.
Virginia Tech Hokies.portal_recruiting: Strong and specifically ranked. Per 247Sports Virginia Tech brought in the conference's fourth-ranked portal class, and the guide says the programme hit the portal for passers and raised talent at virtually every position group.
Virginia Tech Hokies.vsin_assessment: A good fit for this conference, stated with a joke and a caveat. The Coaching Carousel opens by saying it made sure to double-check that Ohio State and Michigan did not move to the ACC before discussing Franklin, calls him a solid motivator, a good recruiter and a pretty lackluster in-game coach, and concludes that the conference lacks premier teams right now so this is a perfect landing spot — a transformation that could and should be quick. The team pages make the same point analytically: Franklin does not often lose games he should win, something that trips up nearly every other ACC programme, with a projection of 7.1 wins.
Virginia Tech Hokies.strengths: A head coach with six double-digit winning seasons and a high regular-season floor who the guide says rarely loses games he should win, the conference's fourth-ranked portal class, 17 returning starters, a retained defensive coordinator with a long association with the head coach, four of the top six tacklers back, and recruiting ties in the DMV and Pennsylvania.
Virginia Tech Hokies.concerns: A Stability Score of 4, an in-game coaching reputation the Carousel calls pretty lackluster, a Penn State pattern of losing to the conference's class, a defense the guide calls uncharacteristically bad at over 30 points allowed, and a schedule including SMU, Clemson and Miami.
Virginia Tech Hokies.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though its projection of 7.1 wins is argued directly from the head coach's record — that he does not often lose games he should win.
Virginia Tech Hokies.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens with a joke that carries his argument: he made sure to double-check that Ohio State and Michigan did not move to the ACC before discussing Franklin. His assessment is three-part and unsparing — a solid motivator, a good recruiter, and a pretty lackluster in-game coach — but he immediately supplies the fit: the conference lacks premier teams right now, and this is a perfect landing spot. He sets out the record: just 8-7 in bowl games and 2-1 in the CFP, with a very high regular-season floor including two 9-4 seasons at Vanderbilt in the early 2010s when that was a rough job, and six double-digit winning seasons at Penn State. He adds that there is a lot of talent in the Hokies' pipeline and that Franklin, a southeastern PA native, should do very well recruiting in the DMV and the Keystone State. His conclusion is that this could be and should be a quick transformation.

Wake Forest Demon Deacons.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Jake Dickert arriving from Washington State and immediately succeeding, and says it rated him there and still does.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.oc: Co-coordinators Rob Ezell and Dan Enos.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.dc: Scottie Hazelton, whom the guide credits with an outstanding job.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide records co-coordinators on offense.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide makes a specific causal link about quarterback mobility instead: Robby Ashford's running meant Wake Forest allowed only 17 sacks after surrendering 91 across the two prior seasons and at least 35 in each of the last four, and notes left-handed Gio Lopez is not that type of player.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Hazelton's unit cutting over 10 points and 1.4 yards per play year over year, finishing ninth nationally in yards per play with a top-10 red zone defense.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide judges Gio Lopez, who had only a 10-to-5 ratio at nearby North Carolina, a very underwhelming addition for co-coordinators Rob Ezell and Dan Enos.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 11 returning starters, totalling 12.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinator positions returning.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.prior_school: Washington State for Dickert. On the roster the guide records Gio Lopez from North Carolina, and notes Robby Ashford was previously at Auburn and South Carolina.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.portal_recruiting: Named as a stated weakness and used to build an argument. The guide cites one of the conference's worst portal hauls, notes Wake Forest has been fundraising well for its NIL budget, and reasons that since it evidently did not have to spend heavily to keep the defense together, it should have aimed higher on offense.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.vsin_assessment: High on the coach, low on the season, and explicit about keeping the two apart. The guide calls Dickert's 9-4 debut one of the more surprising first-year performances, notes the hire met mixed feelings when Dave Clawson amicably parted ways, and says it rated Dickert at Washington State and still does. Separately it lays out a detailed regression case: wins as an underdog over Virginia Tech, SMU and Virginia; a defense tied for 119th in red zone attempts against yet 10th in red zone touchdown percentage; an offense tied for 86th in red zone attempts and 104th in red zone touchdowns; and the most plays of 60-plus yards in the country. It strongly questions the ability to sustain those situational numbers.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.strengths: A head coach the guide rates on his own merits with a surprising 9-4 debut, both coordinator positions returning, a defense that cut over 10 points and 1.4 yards per play to finish ninth nationally, the top pass rusher back, and a healthy NIL fundraising position.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.concerns: An offense the guide calls basically brand new apart from its leading receiver, a quarterback it calls a very underwhelming addition whose immobility removes the mechanism that cut sacks from 91 over two years to 17, a rebuilt offensive line, and one of the conference's worst portal hauls.
Wake Forest Demon Deacons.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide is careful to separate its view of the coach from its view of the season — it rated Dickert at Washington State and still does — and cites the portal haul and lost offensive production as the reasons a downturn should be expected, even with a projection of 6.01 wins.
